title: Endings
summary: Based on resolve, not-taking-it-seriously threshold, whether Xian survives, and the tower rooftop experience, you reach one of five endings.

sharedIntro.speaker: narrator
sharedIntro.text: The broadcast tower shrinks to a red dot behind you. Up ahead the highway splits into several roads that almost look the same—except you know better. There aren't that many choices left.

hidden.speaker: xian
hidden.text: ...Wait. Have you... been saying random stuff this whole time?

hidden.speaker: ringo
hidden.text: I can't do this anymore. Seriously, this road movie is way too long.

hidden.speaker: xian
hidden.text: ...As the writer, I gotta ask: are you tired? Done playing along?

hidden.speaker: narrator
hidden.text: A corner of the green screen peels back. No gunshot, no radio tower—just a few teens looking at each other, deciding to leave set and go get skewers.

hidden.speaker: narrator
hidden.text: [Hidden Ending] When you're not taking it seriously, even tragedy turns into comedy. —Game Over.

bad.speaker: narrator
bad.text: The antibiotics run out. Xian's fever never breaks.

bad.speaker: xian
bad.text: ...Don't cry. I... was always supposed to... stop at the prettiest frame.

bad.speaker: narrator
bad.text: The light goes out in Ringo's eyes. Later you hear they took the violent road—and you couldn't stop it. White light tears the wasteland apart.

bad.speaker: narrator
bad.text: Ten years later. No supernatural, no adults. You're in a black suit at a headstone—Xian's real headstone. The others lost touch long ago. Only you still come.

bad.speaker: narrator
bad.text: In your fantasy, Xian died saving her friends. In reality, she couldn't find a reason to keep living and left on her own. You clutch the wasteland novel you made up, proof you were never a coward.

bad.speaker: narrator
bad.text: [Bad Ending] You turn and walk back into adult life. Wind's loud; the headstone is quiet. —Game Over.

normal.speaker: narrator
normal.text: The tower was empty; the signal was dead. You sat under the stars a long time. Nobody said it was worth it.

normal.speaker: ringo
normal.text: ...The universe doesn't care. We're gonna grow up anyway, right?

normal.speaker: narrator
normal.text: The stars cut out like an old TV yanked from the wall—picture tilts, static dies. You're in a cramped apartment, a tired adult now.

normal.speaker: narrator
normal.text: Email, KPIs, rent. The world didn't get softer—you just stopped asking why.

normal.speaker: narrator
normal.text: Your phone buzzes. Caller ID: Xian.

normal.speaker: narrator
normal.text: You pick up. No miracle, no wasteland—just a familiar breath on the line. You smile, faint and real.

normal.speaker: narrator
normal.text: [Normal Ending] The bond is thin, but it's enough to give you a fixed point in empty days. —Game Over.

good.speaker: narrator
good.text: You heard Teacher calling—and then realized you're still at the campsite where you never found Teacher. Time never really left this night.

good.speaker: narrator
good.text: In the distance, an ugly city glows at night. You're not afraid anymore. The RV, the gunshot, the empty tower—all stories you can tell now.

good.speaker: ringo
good.text: ...Turns out the best loot was the trip itself.

good.speaker: xian
good.text: ...I got it all on film. Everything.

good.speaker: narrator
good.text: The story skips the worst part. Ten years later, millennium campsite—four people around the fire again. All adults this time.

good.speaker: xian
good.text: ...I wrote that year into a novel. Changed a lot. But you're all still in it.

good.speaker: narrator
good.text: Your phone rings—boss blowing up your phone. You hang up and steal the skewer from Ringo's hand. Teen energy and adult life overlap. Not perfect. Enough.

good.speaker: narrator
good.text: [Good Ending] You made peace with an imperfect reality. You think that's all there is. —Game Over?

true.speaker: teacher
true.text: ...You made it. There's nothing on the roof, right?

true.speaker: teacher
true.text: I'm jealous of you imperfect kids—you get to mess up, and you don't have to be perfect.

true.speaker: narrator
true.text: You want to ask something, but deeper wind rolls in—like a night on an unfinished building, like some almost-jump moment in 199X.

true.speaker: narrator
true.text: Camp, Teacher, the four-person trip—some of it happened, some got written in later. But the running away and staying together back then was real.

true.speaker: ringo
true.text: ...The journey is the answer. We made it here.

true.speaker: narrator
true.text: The fire goes out. Pure white rises. The cast stands in everyday clothes like beginners at acting—a little stiff, a little real.

true.speaker: xian
true.text: ...In the script I wrote, I was supposed to die no matter what.

true.speaker: xian
true.text: It was you. Your choices—messy, illogical—tore that ending up.

true.speaker: narrator
true.text: Xian walks to the edge of the light, raises her old camera, and looks straight at you on the other side of the screen. Shutter click.

true.speaker: xian
true.text: This film is for you. Stay noisy. Stay yourself.

true.speaker: narrator
true.text: [True Ending] Credits roll. The light fades. —Game Over.
